{{Quote|You may be the hottest bush pilot this side of Mos Eisley, Luke, but those little skyhoppers can be dangerous. They move awfully fast for tropospheric craft&mdash;faster than they need to. Keep playing engine jockey with one and someday, whammo! You're going to be nothing more than a dark spot on the damp side of a canyon wall.|[[Biggs Darklighter/Legends|Biggs Darklighter]], to [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]|<ref name="Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope (novel)">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' novel]]</ref>}}
The '''T-16 skyhopper''' was a high-performance [[Airspeeder/Legends|airspeeder]].

==Characteristics==
[[File:Skyhopper_egvv.jpg|thumb|left|180px|T-16 schematics.]]
{{Quote|T-16s are a lot like the snubfighters we're using.''"<br />"''I know, I looked one over. I'm sure I can handle it.|Biggs Darklighter and Luke Skywalker, before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]|<ref name="Case for Rebellion">{{SWRadio|The Case for Rebellion}}</ref>}}
The [[Incom Corporation/Legends|Incom Corporation]] T-16 [[Airspeeder/Legends|Skyhopper]] was equipped with an [[Ion engine/Legends|ion drive]]<ref name="RS I guide">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron: The Official Nintendo Player's Guide]]''</ref> and a fully pressurized cockpit, allowing it to operate at trans-orbital altitudes.

Civilian versions of the skyhopper were armed with [[Pneumatic cannon/Legends|pneumatic cannons]], and were equipped with [[Targeting laser/Legends|targeting lasers]]<ref name="RS I guide" /> though many law-enforcement agencies and [[Planet/Legends|planetary]] militaries throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] utilized modified T-16s due to their overall good performance. However, because it was armed with only a single mounted [[Repeating blaster/Legends|repeating blaster]], it was often overlooked by the military.

Even so, these airspeeders were often used as training vehicles by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]],<ref name="Star Wars: Rebel Assault">''[[Star Wars: Rebel Assault]]''</ref> due to the fact that their flight controls were similar to those of [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wings]].

The skyhopper was a common sight across the galaxy, with versions of the craft found on nearly every settled world. The T-16 was identified by its tri-wing design and triangular cabin. The three wings, which were reproduced in countless [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Transport/Legends|transports]], provided excellent stability. The central airfoil segmented the canopy and blocked much of the pilot's view, but computer displays and a holographic mapping system compensated for this decreased field of view.

The speeder had a top speed of approximately 1,200 [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] per [[Standard hour/Legends|hour]], and the two [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsor generators]] provided lift up to 300 meters.<ref name="RS I guide" /> Many young [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] preferred skyhoppers over [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeders]] because of the increased maneuverability.

==History==
[[Kodo Arr]], the self-proclaimed "galaxy's best smuggler", owned a T-16. He claimed that if you put a "hundred large" credits into it, it could become a great craft. He once smuggled a box larger than the speeder on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]], which almost broke the craft.<ref name="Smuggler">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/livingforce/swlf20040219smuggler|text=Smuggler's Trade|int=Smuggler's Trade}}</ref>

In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] [[Anchorhead Base]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] used T-16 for trainee pilots through the nearby [[Beggar's Canyon/Legends|Beggar's Canyon]]. [[Merrick Simms]] flew under the [[Callsign/Legends|call sign]] [[Green Leader/Legends|Green Leader]] and trained pilots such as "[[Rookie One]]".<ref name="RA">''[[Star Wars: Rebel Assault]]''</ref><ref name="RATOIG">''[[Star Wars: Rebel Assault: The Official Insider's Guide]]''</ref>

[[File:T-16_Skyhopper_TCG-TT.png|thumb|left|180px|T-16 in landing configuration.]]
[[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] owned a [[Luke's T-16 skyhopper/Legends|T-16]] on his home planet of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], where he would use [[Womp rat/Legends|womp rats]] as target practice and race through [[Beggar's Canyon/Legends|Beggar's Canyon]] with his friend, [[Biggs Darklighter/Legends|Biggs Darklighter]]<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref>. After an incident where Skywalker "threaded the needle" during a dangerous run through Beggar's Canyon, the T-16 ended up undergoing repairs at the Lars Homestead, repairs that were ultimately not completed by the time of the [[Battle of Tatooine (Galactic Civil War)|battle]] between the [[Tantive IV/Legends|''Tantive IV'']] and the [[Devastator/Legends|''Devastator'']]<ref name="SW:CL">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref>.

Six [[Standard month/Legends|months]] after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]],<ref name="RS I guide" /> two T-16s were flying through Beggar's Canyon when the Empire [[Ambush at Mos Eisley|raided]] [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]].<ref name="RS I">[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']]</ref>

The [[MT-16]] was a T-16 modified by the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] with a [[Blaster cannon/Legends|blaster cannon]] for light combat<ref name="HTTESB">''[[Heir to the Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref>.

==Behind the scenes==
In [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']], Luke is seen playing with a model of a T-16, which in reality was the prop miniature built by [[Colin Cantwell]]. The actual prop could not be completed, and an incomplete model can be seen in the background of the droid cleaning scene. The [[Star Wars (radio)|radio]] episode "[[A Wind to Shake the Stars]]" later depicted Luke damaging his T-16 in a race through Beggar's Canyon, and therefore he had to search for [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] in his landspeeder.<ref name="A Wind">{{SWRadio|A Wind to Shake the Stars}}</ref> The skyhopper's engine was one of the few original sound effects that had to be created for the radio drama rather than remixed from the film's sound library.<ref name="Bantha">{{BanthaCite|11|S.W. on N.P.R.}}</ref>

[[File:T-16_Skyhopper_Sketchbook.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Early T-16 concept sketch]]
A flying T-16 can be seen above [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] during the [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']] [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|Special Edition's]] celebration ending sequence.

In [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Attack of the Clones'']], a T-16 can be seen in the background of the homestead garage scene.

In the [[1998]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']], the first bonus mission is a T-16 skyhopper race between the player (Luke Skywalker), [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]], [[Zev Senesca/Legends|Zev Senesca]], and [[Dak Ralter/Legends|Dak Ralter]]. In the game's sequels ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader]]'' and ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]'', the player flies a T-16 for the [[Canon|non-canon]] training.

Some of the speeder points (flight paths, in MMO terms) in the [[2011]] video game ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' use a vehicle of similar design - also referred to as a [[Skyhopper/Legends|skyhopper]] - to travel to various points. The skyhopper is most often used on [[Balmorra/Legends|Balmorra]] and [[Voss]], due to their largely mountainous terrains that inhibit the use of regular speeders.
